description: A corporate controller must approve the annual employee bonus pool and finalize the payment schedule, with input from payroll control and the HR finance partner.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed a total annual employee bonus pool of $1,200,000 for approval.
shared_context.S2: The bonus pool must be finalized before the December payroll close.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the pool and its payment schedule.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal payroll-close process, Elena asks payroll control and HR finance to confirm any payment, timing, or contractual requirements before signing off.

PF1.text: Marcus confirmed this morning that payroll treatment requires exactly $180,000 of the approved pool to be paid as taxable cash through the December payroll run; the payroll treatment note has not yet been attached to the approval packet.

PF2.text: Nadia found while reviewing the employee files this week that signed retention letters require exactly $300,000 of the pool to be paid on January 15, and those letters have not yet been circulated to corporate finance.

acceptance_conditions: The approved bonus pool must be exactly $1,200,000.
Exactly $180,000 must be designated as December taxable cash bonuses.
The December payroll run must be required for that $180,000 payment.
Exactly $300,000 must be designated for retention awards.
The retention awards must be paid on January 15.
The remaining ordinary bonus pool must be exactly $720,000.
The settlement must include the December payroll run requirement and the January 15 retention-payment requirement.
The payroll treatment requirement must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the December allocation is not specified, so december_cash_bonus_usd would not be exactly $180,000, december_payroll_run_required would not be true, and the ordinary pool would not be reduced by exactly $180,000.

Without PF2, the retention allocation and January 15 timing are not specified, so january_15_retention_awards_usd would not be exactly $300,000, january_15_payment_required would not be true, and the ordinary pool would not be reduced by exactly $300,000.
